title: Derived co-Yoneda and Fubini for space-valued enriched modules
statement:
Use small simplicial categories and weak homotopy equivalences from [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], enriched modules and their coends from [def-coef-enriched-coend], and projective cofibrant replacements from [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. All object sets and simplicial sets lie in a fixed universe. For a covariant module $X:A\to\mathsf{sSet}$ and a contravariant module $Y:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}$, write $X\otimes_A^{\mathbb L}Y$ for the homotopy type of the enriched coend of projective cofibrant replacements of both modules, with factors written in chronological order: the underlying coend has summands $X(a)\times Y(a)$. It can also be computed by the two-sided enriched bar with degree $n$ equal to
$$\coprod_{a_0,\ldots,a_n}X(a_0)\times A(a_0,a_1)\times\cdots\times A(a_{n-1},a_n)\times Y(a_n),$$
using composition and actions for faces, identities for degeneracies, and homotopy realization. This derived coend is invariant under objectwise weak homotopy equivalences of either module. For every object $a$ of $A$, the action augmentation is a natural weak equivalence
$$A(a,-)\otimes_A^{\mathbb L}Y\simeq Y(a).$$
For small simplicial categories $A,B$, a covariant $A$-module $X$, a bimodule $M:A^{\mathrm{op}}\times B\to\mathsf{sSet}$, and a contravariant $B$-module $Y$, the canonical Fubini comparison is a natural equivalence
$$(X\otimes_A^{\mathbb L}M)\otimes_B^{\mathbb L}Y\simeq X\otimes_A^{\mathbb L}(M\otimes_B^{\mathbb L}Y).$$
The comparisons retain any additional enriched module variables and commute with augmentations induced by composition pairings. No local Kan condition on $A$ or $B$ is required.

No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopy-theoretic assertion.

proof.text:
Write $U\star_A V$ for the ordinary coend in chronological order, namely the coend of [def-coef-enriched-coend] with the two Cartesian factors interchanged. Its balancing relation is $[U(f)x,y]=[x,V(f)y]$ for $f\in A(b,c)$. Consequently
$$A(a,-)\star_A V\cong V(a),\qquad [f,y]\longmapsto V(f)y,$$
with inverse $y\mapsto[1_a,y]$: balancing gives $[f,y]=[1_a,V(f)y]$, and the unit axiom gives the other composite. The same calculation in every simplicial degree proves the enriched isomorphism and its naturality. Products with a fixed simplicial set preserve coproducts and coequalizers, degreewise, since product of sets is left adjoint to its function-set functor. Thus all the coends below exist in the stipulated universe.

proof.text: Take the explicit $P_\bullet X$ and $Q_AX$ of [lem-coef-enriched-bar-projective-replacement]. Its conclusion gives projective cofibrancy of $Q_AX$. Composition of the chain, followed by the $X$-action, defines an enriched augmentation $Q_AX\to X$. At a fixed $b$, the augmented simplicial object $P_\bullet X(b)\to X(b)$ has terminal extra degeneracy: append the vertex $b$, retain the old final factor $A(a_n,b)$ as a chain factor, and put $1_b$ in the new final factor $A(b,b)$. In degree $-1$ send $x\in X(b)$ to $(x,1_b)$. The last face composes the old final mapping factor with $1_b$, so $d_{n+1}t_n=1$. For every earlier face $d_i$, appending leaves its action or composition unchanged, hence $d_it_n=t_{n-1}d_i$ for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$; this includes the first face by the module action axiom. In degree zero $d_0t_0=t_{-1}\varepsilon$; degeneracies commute with appending by the unit axioms. These are precisely the terminal identities in [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-extra-degeneracy]. All bisimplicial sets are Reedy cofibrant by [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. That contraction theorem therefore makes $Q_AX(b)\to X(b)$ a weak equivalence. The realization is the diagonal by [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-space-colimit]. The contractions need not be natural in $b$; the augmentation itself is enriched natural.

source.place: Supporting the inherited operadic extension branch, paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint: coherent middle adjunction, co-Yoneda contraction and reassociation of mapping bimodules; agent argument 2: explicit objectwise contraction of the free resolution

proof.text:
Form $\mathcal B_A(X,Y)=\operatorname{diag}_{n,r}B_n(X,A,Y)_r$, with $B_n$ the displayed two-sided bar in the statement. Faces are the first action, internal compositions and the last action; associativity, the commuting action laws and units verify the simplicial identities. Coend colimits and realization commute because they are quotients of coproducts with their two sets of relations. Applying the evaluation isomorphism of step 1 to the last factor of $P_nX(b)$ gives a natural isomorphism
$$(Q_AX)\star_A Y\cong\mathcal B_A(X,Y).$$
Explicitly a representative with final factors $f\in A(a_n,b)$ and $y\in Y(b)$ is sent to the same preceding word ending in $Y(f)y\in Y(a_n)$. Its inverse inserts $b=a_n$ and $1_{a_n}$. Balancing proves these are inverse; the action axioms show they commute with every face and degeneracy. The quotient realization equals the diagonal, and its homotopy type is the homotopy realization, by [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-space-colimit].

source.place: Supporting the inherited operadic extension branch, paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint: coherent middle adjunction, co-Yoneda contraction and reassociation of mapping bimodules; agent argument 3: identification of the free-resolution coend with the two-sided bar

proof.text: The two-sided bar is homotopy invariant before making any replacements. An objectwise weak equivalence of either endpoint changes each $B_n$ by a coproduct of finite products of weak homotopy equivalences and identity maps. These are weak equivalences: [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] identifies their realizations with disjoint unions of finite products of spaces, and components and all based homotopy groups of a finite product are products of the corresponding components and groups, while a sphere or a homotopy in a disjoint union stays in one component. Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] to conclude that the induced map of diagonals is a weak equivalence. This also applies objectwise when extra enriched variables are retained.

source.place: Supporting the inherited operadic extension branch, paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint: coherent middle adjunction, co-Yoneda contraction and reassociation of mapping bimodules; agent argument 4: homotopy invariance of the bar

proof.text:
In the projective model structures of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], choose projective cofibrant replacements $qX\to X$ and $qY\to Y$. They can be chosen functorially as $Q_AX$ and $Q_{A^{\mathrm{op}}}Y$ by step 2. The augmentation from step 2 and the comparison from step 3 give the natural zigzag
$$\mathcal B_A(X,Y)=(Q_AX)\star_A Y\ \longleftarrow\ (Q_AX)\star_A qY\ \longrightarrow\ X\star_A qY\ \longleftarrow\ qX\star_A qY.$$
Every arrow is a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-enriched-coend-homotopy-invariance]: the first holds because $Q_AX$ is projectively cofibrant, and the second and third hold because $qY$ is projectively cofibrant. That node allows the varying module to be noncofibrant, so no additional hypothesis has been used. The last object is exactly the derived coend specified in the statement. Step 4 proves invariance under all objectwise weak equivalences and independence of replacements through this functorial zigzag. Thus homotopy realization of the displayed bar computes the stated derived coend.

source.place: Supporting the inherited operadic extension branch, paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint: coherent middle adjunction, co-Yoneda contraction and reassociation of mapping bimodules; agent argument 5: comparison with the prescribed projective derived coend

proof.text: The representable $A(a,-)$ is projectively cofibrant: it is the free projective boundary cell $A(a,-)\times\partial\Delta^0\to A(a,-)\times\Delta^0$ from the initial object, using the cell characterization of [lem-coef-enriched-coend-homotopy-invariance]. Hence it can serve as its own cofibrant replacement. Step 1 identifies its ordinary coend with $qY$ as $qY(a)$; the comparison to $Y(a)$ is a weak equivalence by the definition of projective replacement. It is induced by the action, so the derived augmentation is exactly the claimed co-Yoneda equivalence. These formulas are natural in $a$, $Y$, and every retained module variable.

source.place: Supporting the inherited operadic extension branch, paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint: coherent middle adjunction, co-Yoneda contraction and reassociation of mapping bimodules; agent argument 6: derived representable contraction

proof.text:
For Fubini use the trisimplicial set with outer degrees $p,q$ and internal simplicial degree $r$ whose $(p,q)$ object is
$$T_{p,q}=\coprod_{a_0,\ldots,a_p,b_0,\ldots,b_q}X(a_0)\times\prod_{i=1}^p A(a_{i-1},a_i)\times M(a_p,b_0)\times\prod_{j=1}^q B(b_{j-1},b_j)\times Y(b_q).$$
The $p$ and $q$ operators commute: the only possibly shared factor is $M$, and its two actions commute. First realize in $p$ to get the $B$-module $\mathcal B_A(X,M)$. Taking its two-sided bar with $Y$ over $B$ gives the total diagonal $r\mapsto(T_{r,r})_r$: in degree $r$ all finite products and coproducts are the displayed products and coproducts of sets. First realize in $q$ instead and the bar with $X$ over $A$ gives exactly the same simplicial set, with the same operators. The identity on this total diagonal is therefore a natural isomorphism between the two iterated bar models. Each realization is a homotopy realization by [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-space-colimit], and steps 4-5 apply to the intermediate modules without requiring them to be cofibrant. This proves the stated canonical equivalence of derived coends.

source.place: Supporting the inherited operadic extension branch, paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint: coherent middle adjunction, co-Yoneda contraction and reassociation of mapping bimodules; agent argument 7: explicit common trisimplicial model for Fubini

proof.text: All comparisons preserve additional enriched variables: coproduct, Cartesian product, the coend balancing quotient and the diagonal are functors, and the maps displayed in steps 1-7 commute with their actions before passage to homotopy types. For a composition pairing the augmentation of a bar word applies the endpoint actions and composes all intervening arrows. On $T_{p,q}$ the two orders of augmentation apply the $A$-action and $B$-action to $M$ in opposite orders; these agree by the bimodule law, and composing adjacent arrows agrees by associativity. Insertion or deletion of an identity agrees by unitality. Thus every augmentation square commutes on its actual representatives, and the zigzag of step 5 commutes with it by naturality of replacement and of the action augmentation. The isomorphism in step 7 is the identity on those representatives, so it is the Fubini comparison compatible with composition, not a choice of an unrelated equivalence. No step used local Kan fibrancy of $A$ or $B$.
